work_order: WO: groq-api Kernel compose (Lane B Cursor), 2026-09-04
lane: Cursor Cloud Agent, Opus 5 (Composer 2.5 / Auto refused by the work order)
protocol: P10 PROPOSE — nothing here is wired; CCr writes the live tree

satellite.instruction: NOT rewritten. This record proposes the ATTACH the satellite is missing, plus the seven invariants the attach depends on. proposals/groq_compose_ref.py::conformance() checks the live satellite against them.

tier.why_it_matters: The two constraints in the work order — no service_tier=flex, and refuse Mixtral / Llama 3.x Free-Dev ids — are the same fact wearing two hats: this key is not on a committed-spend contract. Flex is paid-accounts-only (498 capacity_exceeded), and Groq's 2026-08-16 notice scopes the Llama 3.x retirement to 'free and developer-tier usage; enterprise customers with a committed-spend contract are not affected'. Encoding them as two unrelated hard-coded lists is how they drift apart. One declared tier drives both.
tier.second_reason_flex_stays_refused: Flex's own contract is 'fails fast with 498, add jittered backoff and retries'. cosmos_sched is report-never-retry (cosmos_sched.py:18). A rail that needs client-side retry to meet its contract cannot be driven by a scheduler that refuses to retry. Upgrading the key does not remove this reason.

refusals_family_net: On free/developer, any unlisted Llama 3.x or Mixtral spelling is refused as well. A dated table is a cache of the vendor's catalog and goes stale silently, which is fail-open; the family net covers the Llama/Mixtral part of that window and GroqRail.probe_deep() covers the rest against GET /openai/v1/models, which consumes no tokens.

invariants.statement: compose is in-memory; a read-only kernel appends nothing at boot
invariants.enforced_by: attach_groq_rail(read_only=True) returns after adapters[link]=rail and attach_probe; Registry.register (LINK_REGISTERED) and SpendGate.set_budget (BUDGET_SET) are skipped
invariants.risk_if_broken: the B1 scar reopens — `cosmos status` beside `serve` becomes a second writer, two appends per boot

invariants.statement: register/budget are idempotent - a re-boot must not re-register, because LINK_REGISTERED discards the last probe and unroutes the link
invariants.enforced_by: attach checks registry.state() and spend.audit() first; the register goes through ledger.append_guarded so two kernels booting at once cannot both write
invariants.risk_if_broken: MEASURED in this clone: register -> probe -> register leaves matrix() verified=None and route('core','models') == []. Every composed rail becomes permanently unroutable on a box that boots Core often.

invariants.statement: refused model ids are refused LOCALLY, before key and socket, tier-scoped
invariants.enforced_by: check_model() runs first in build_request(); refusal carries the shutdown date and the replacement id
invariants.risk_if_broken: a round trip that can only fail, and an error message from the wire that names neither the date nor the replacement

invariants.statement: service_tier never reaches the body; a caller-supplied one is refused
invariants.enforced_by: FORBIDDEN_PARAMS refuses it (PARAM_REFUSED) and PASSTHROUGH_PARAMS is an allow-list, so omission — which IS on_demand — cannot be edited into flex by accident
invariants.risk_if_broken: 498 capacity_exceeded on a free key, and a retry requirement the scheduler refuses to meet

invariants.statement: response.model is bound, and the SERVED id is re-checked against the table
invariants.enforced_by: bind_served_model() reads data['model'], reports drift, and re-runs check_model on the served id -> MODEL_DRIFT
invariants.risk_if_broken: a permitted request answered by a retired model reads as a clean success; SOP.md: read state back after every write

invariants.statement: the credential never reaches a ledger payload, an error, or a result
invariants.enforced_by: key resolved at dispatch time only; redact() applied to every detail string before it can be carried
invariants.risk_if_broken: the authority ledger is an append-only hash chain with no delete — a secret written once is written forever, and removing it afterwards breaks the chain

invariants.statement: no socket without an injected transport; construction opens nothing
invariants.enforced_by: transport injected at the composition boundary exactly as cosmos_kernel injects _https_get into ITC; construction reads no key and imports nothing optional
invariants.risk_if_broken: composition can fail, and a rail that will not compose takes Core down with it

groq-api rail attach.reason: the satellite becomes a rail adapter reachable through the Dispatcher on the core->models route, exactly as bts_sgh/gem/gw/oa_api did; attach mirrors cosmos_node_rails.register_node_rails so the port is mechanical

boot composition.reason: four lines under the existing boot_compose block: an adapter map, a guarded call, and a typed record on failure. The Kernel gains no Groq fact of its own — no endpoint, no model id, no refusal list — so there is no second declaration to drift

groq-api spend accounting.reason: metered_usd nonzero so cosmos_rails routes the call through the breaker at all; settles UNPRICED because Groq bills tokens, not dollars. A LOCAL refusal settles at a measured $0.00 instead, since a call that never left the process did not happen at an unknown price

groq-api liveness.reason: shallow probe on the Registry (credential + permitted default model, zero requests, two ways to go red); deep catalog probe on the health board, because Registry.probe_all() is reached from status paths and a network fan-out there turns `cosmos status` into an egress event

transport.reason: the injected-fetcher seam ITC already uses, for the same stated reason: the module never opens the network itself, so no code path a test exercises can silently depend on reachability. Tests stay fake-HTTP with no mocking library

service_tier=flex.reason: paid-accounts-only (498 capacity_exceeded on this key) AND its contract requires client-side jittered retry, which cosmos_sched refuses by design. Omitting the field selects on_demand

Mixtral and Llama 3.x free/dev model ids.reason: retired by the vendor on dated notices; refused locally with the date and the replacement rather than round-tripped into a 400 model_decommissioned

kernel_patch.shape: self.adapters = {}; if boot_compose: compose_into_kernel(self) — wrapped so a rail that will not compose cannot stop Core reaching READY

recommended_but_not_applied.cosmos_registry.register_once: Registry.register() offers no guarded variant, so the attach restates the LINK_REGISTERED payload to get an atomic check-then-append. Restating a contract in a second place is the drift this tree keeps closing. The durable fix is a register_once() on the Registry; until then the restatement is compared byte-for-byte against what Registry.register() writes, in the test.
recommended_but_not_applied.cosmos_rails fallback kinds: Dispatcher continues to the next live link only for UNREACHABLE / SESSION_EXPIRED / AUTH_REQUIRED. RATE_LIMITED (429) is arguably a fourth, but widening that set changes routing for every rail, so it is named here and not done.

open_questions: Which tier is the live key actually on? Everything above assumes free/developer, fail-closed. An enterprise committed-spend key legitimately keeps llama-3.3-70b-versatile and llama-3.1-8b-instant, and a blanket refusal would be wrong for it.

Does the live satellite already expose probe()/dispatch() in the tree's adapter shape, or does it expose ask() like the bts_* incumbents? If ask(), the attach wraps it in a NodeRail-style shim and nothing else changes.

Does the live Kernel's boot_compose block call a single attach function per rail (the firecrawl/cursor shape), or one combined register_*_rails()? Neither is visible from this clone; the attach signature mirrors register_node_rails so either lands.

Where does the live tree resolve GROQ_API_KEY — environment, config/secrets, or the .secrets file cosmos_port_plan names for bts_cursor? The reference reads the environment and never captures at import; the file provider is one function.
Should groq-api share the model-rail budget or hold its own? It holds its own $5 cap here, which makes it visible in spend.audit() as a separate row.
falsification: If a read-only Kernel appends anything at boot after this lands, I1 is broken and the B1 scar is back: compare len(list(k.ledger.verify())) across Kernel(root, read_only=True) with and without boot_compose.
If `cosmos status` shows groq-api verified=None after Core has been up and probed, I2 is broken — something is re-registering on every boot.
If any SPEND_SETTLED for groq-api carries measured_usd 0.0 for a call that actually reached the API, the UNPRICED rule is being violated in the direction that hides spend.
If a 498 ever appears in the ledger, something re-enabled service_tier.
If grep of the authority ledger finds the key prefix, I6 is broken and the chain cannot be repaired — rotate the key, do not edit the ledger.
